title: Fastpath lint reroute, dependency visibility audit, and lightweight presubmit telemetry
author: Ethan Wang
description: Context and motivation: Our presubmit lane has two pain points: 1) developers hit long lint feedback times because lint shards are pinned to heavyweight runners; 2) dependency visibility is poor in presubmit which creates noisy failures and blocked merges. This PR introduces a light-weight 'fastpath' presubmit router, augments dependency visibility telemetry, and performs a small audit of top-level deps to reduce spurious infra noise. Summary of changes: - Introduce a presubmit router that routes small lint-only PRs to lightweight ephemeral runners (fastpath) and leaves heavier integration flows untouched. - Add dependency-visibility telemetry hooks (dep fingerprinting and top-level dep list) to CI traces and to the local dev lint script. - Replace the monolithic .github/presubmit.yml with two focused workflows: presubmit-fastpath.yml and presubmit-standard.yml. - Add a small dep-audit utility under tools/dep-audit to build a top-level manifest used by the router and for telemetry. - Update dev docs with quickstart for fastpath and fallback flows. Checklist: - [x] Fastpath router implementation and unit tests - [x] CI workflow split and smoke runs - [x] Dep-audit utility and packaging script - [x] Docs + migration notes - [x] Feature gated behind repo-level flag (default: enabled for files < 200 LOC and changes restricted to src/, pkg/, docs/) Rollout plan: 1) Feature enabled in main for all internal builds behind a repo flag. 2) Observe telemetry for one week; measure median lint feedback latency and presubmit success rate. 3) If no regressions, enable by default for all fastpath-eligible PRs. Backwards compatibility / migration: Existing presubmit logic stays in presubmit-standard.yml and is the default for non-eligible PRs. Dep-audit can be run locally (tools/dep-audit scan) to generate the manifest for a developer; CI will regenerate on every run. Testing and validation: Ran full CI matrix in ephemeral environment (see CI notes). Manually validated that lint responses for small PRs dropped from ~7m to ~90s median in the canary org. Related linear: ENG-1245 implements telemetry contract; ENG-2033 tracks router heuristics and rollout. Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the router decision heuristic conservative; if the heuristics are too restrictive we'll relax them in a follow-up. For incident mitigation, presubmit-standard.yml remains the clear fallback.
commits: router: add fastpath presubmit router and tests
ci: split presubmit into presubmit-fastpath and presubmit-standard
tools/dep-audit: add manifest generator and fingerprinting
docs: presubmit fastpath quickstart and rollback notes

Sofia Martinez: Can you add CI budget telemetry for fastpath vs standard so SRE can track cost variance?
Liam O'Connor: Minor nits in shellscript quoting; also prefer a smaller docker image for fastpath runner — suggested alpine + busybox.

Ethan Wang (author): Addressed Priya's test note and added a unit that simulates proto delta detection. Added telemetry metrics as requested by Sofia (ci.fastpath.count, ci.fastpath.median_latency). Switched fastpath runner image to slim-builder:alpine-3.19. Ready for final review.
release_notes: Introduces fastpath presubmit routing to reduce lint latency on small PRs; adds dep visibility telemetry and a dep-audit tool. No breaking API changes. Rollout behind a repo flag.
